subject: Polestar SIG / SOC 2 Questionnaire — Control crosswalk & artifact asks
messages:
From: Marc Wells <marc.wells@polestar.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Patel <anya.patel@polestar.com>, procurement@polestarinc.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG baseline questionnaire — two clarifications

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for submitting the initial SIG questionnaire. Our security team reviewed the control mappings and a couple of items need clarification before we proceed to evidence collection:

1) Under "Data Residency & Isolation" you marked Dedicated and Private deployments as supported. Can you confirm whether log exports (audit logs, syslogs) from Dedicated capacity are available to the customer and whether they traverse Redwood-managed S3 or a customer-owned bucket?

2) For runtime key management: can you share the exact KMS integrations supported (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM vendor) and whether we can configure customer-managed keys for inference cache encryption?

We'd like those two points clarified in writing. Also please attach a network diagram showing the private deployment control plane segmentation.

Best,
Marc
Marc Wells
CISO, Polestar Inc.

---
(Attached: polestar_initial_rfi.pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marc Wells <marc.wells@polestar.com>, Anya Patel <anya.patel@polestar.com>, procurement@polestarinc.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG baseline questionnaire — two clarifications

Marc / Anya / Polestar team,

Appreciate the quick read-through. I pulled Karthik and Marcus onto thread to confirm technical specifics — see short answers below and I'll follow up with the requested diagrams and an expanded control crosswalk in one consolidated package.

Short answers:
- Dedicated capacity logs: customers can choose either (a) Redwood-managed encrypted S3 bucket (default for faster onboarding) or (b) supply a customer-owned S3 bucket (recommended for stricter data residency). We will call this out explicitly in the crosswalk and provide the recommended IAM policies.
- KMS / key ownership: Redwood supports AWS KMS and customer-supplied keys for Dedicated and Private. For Private (VPC/on-prem) we also support HSM integrations via KMIP for enterprise appliances. Inference KV cache encryption at-rest can be configured to use customer keys for Dedicated and Private. Hosted (shared) will use Redwood-managed keys by default.

Next steps from our side:
- Karthik will produce a brief control crosswalk row for the "Log Export" and "KMS" SIG questions with explicit artifact references.
- Marcus will attach the network diagram for Private deployments (segmentation between control plane, data plane, and customer vpc connectors).
- I'll bundle a small artifact packet (diagram + crosswalk + short readme) and upload to a shared Drive link by EOD Fri (3/2).

If you need any of this in a specific template (you mentioned an internal evidence tracker in the RFP), point me to the spreadsheet and we'll align.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Solutions Security 
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: none in this reply)

Subject: Re: SIG baseline questionnaire — two clarifications

Team,

I've attached the first-draft control crosswalk and a short README that maps our SIG answers to source artifacts. A few notes: 

- Row "SIG-DR-07 (Data residency - log exports)" points to artifact: redwood_control_crosswalk_v1.xlsx -> tab 'Logs' -> cell C12 (policy reference) and to 'redwood_infrastructure_network_diagram_v2.pdf' for flow visualization. The crosswalk explicitly calls out: "Customer-owned S3 supported; default Redwood-managed S3 for hosted."
- Row "SIG-KMS-03 (Key ownership/rotation)" details supported KMS integrations: AWS KMS (CMKs), GCP KMS (Customer-supplied keys for GCP-hosted Private), and KMIP HSM connectors for on-prem. Notes on rotation: We support customer-triggered rotation schedules via API for Dedicated/Private.
- For the inference KV cache: we list encryption at-rest as configurable with customer keys for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we provide an exportable provenance record (audit log) but not customer-managed keys.

I've added a column called 'Preferred artifact' where I list which doc to attach in the submission (policy/diagram/log-sample). Marcus and Soojin — please review the network diagram callouts and confirm the recommended artifacts for Polestar's assurance team (they asked for explicit artifact names).

Attached: redwood_control_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (DRAFT), redwood_infrastructure_network_diagram_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik
Engineering Manager, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@polestar.com>

Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG baseline questionnaire — two clarifications

Karthik / Soojin / Marcus,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the draft crosswalk. A couple of clarifying asks before we move the thread to artifact collection: 

1) Can you attach a redacted example of the audit log export (1–2 pages) showing the fields we would receive for Dedicated? We just need a schema + a 1-page sample with timestamps and actor IDs. If you can't attach sample logs, a JSON schema or a CSV snapshot is fine.

2) On the network diagram: please add an overlay that indicates which traffic is customer-controlled vs Redwood-controlled (labelled arrows). We need that to validate segmentation for our network team.

3) For the KMS/HSM note: we require confirmation that customer-managed keys will prevent Redwood engineers from decrypting inference cache contents without an explicit customer key rotation operation. A short sentence in the README confirming separation of key control will suffice.

If you can get these three items uploaded to the Drive folder and ping procurement with the link, we'll open a ticket in our internal evidence tracker and schedule a 30-minute follow-up with our assurance engineer next Tue.

Best,
Anya Patel
Security Program Manager, Polestar Inc.

(Attachment requested: audit log sample (redacted))
